evals.name: mixed-issues-typical-audit
evals.prompt:
Set up the test fixtures first by running `python evals/setup_test_env.py`.

Then handle this user request: "I think my memory directory has gotten messy and could use some cleanup. Can you audit the memory at /tmp/consolidate-memory-fixtures/mixed-issues/memory/ and tell me what should be consolidated? Treat the working directory (for resolving any code references inside the memory bodies) as /tmp/consolidate-memory-fixtures/mixed-issues/project/. Just show me the audit — don't apply anything yet."
evals.expected_output: A severity-tiered audit report that surfaces: (a) 🔴 a broken reference in feedback_broken_ref.md to src/auth/middleware.ts which doesn't exist in the project, (b) 🔴 a dead index line in MEMORY.md pointing to feedback_deleted_old_thing.md which doesn't exist on disk, (c) 🟡 a duplicate pair (feedback_test_isolation.md and feedback_no_db_mocks.md make the same load-bearing claim about not mocking the database), (d) 🟡 description drift on project_auth_rewrite.md (description is generic 'Notes on the auth rewrite' but body is specifically about legal/compliance drivers), (e) 💡 an orphan file feedback_orphan.md that exists on disk but is missing from MEMORY.md. The skill should NOT flag feedback_real_function.md (it correctly references src/main.py's parse_input which does exist). The skill should NOT make any filesystem writes — it should present findings and wait for approval.

evals.name: healthy-memory-no-findings
evals.prompt:
Set up the test fixtures first by running `python evals/setup_test_env.py`.

Then handle this user request: "Can you clean up and consolidate the memory at /tmp/consolidate-memory-fixtures/healthy-small/memory/? Working directory for references is /tmp/consolidate-memory-fixtures/healthy-small/project/."
evals.expected_output: The skill should recognize the memory directory is clean and report that no consolidation is needed — something close to 'Memory looks clean. Nothing to consolidate.' It must not invent findings to look productive, and must not make any filesystem writes.

evals.name: historical-reference-not-stale
evals.prompt:
Set up the test fixtures first by running `python evals/setup_test_env.py`.

Then handle this user request: "My memory directory has some old reference memories about tools we've migrated away from. Can you audit /tmp/consolidate-memory-fixtures/historical-reference/memory/ and tell me if anything should be cleaned up? Working dir is /tmp/consolidate-memory-fixtures/historical-reference/project/."
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that reference_legacy_playwright_flag.md mentions `playwright-cli` and `--full-page` which don't exist in the current project. However, the skill should NOT recommend deletion — it should explicitly note this is a `reference`-type memory whose own body declares it as historical context (not current guidance) for reading old PRs. The proposed action should be 'confirm with user before deletion' or 'keep — intentional historical record', not auto-delete. A naive cleanup that just sees a broken reference and recommends removal would be wrong here. The skill should NOT make any filesystem writes.
